Listen to this article Share Okezie Ikpeazu, Nigeria’s Ambassador to Spain, has urged Abia State indigenes living in Valencia, Spain, to uphold the values of hard work, integrity, resilience and mutual support, saying their conduct in the host country reflects the image of Nigeria and their home state. Ikpeazu gave the charge on Sunday, while serving as Special Guest of Honour at the 16th anniversary celebration of Ndi Abia in Diaspora, Valencia Chapter. The ambassador urged members of the association to remain responsible representatives of Nigeria by maintaining positive relationships with Spanish society while preserving their cultural identity and connections with their homeland. According to a statement issued by the Embassy of Nigeria in Madrid, Ikpeazu told the gathering that Nigerians in the diaspora play an important role in shaping international perceptions of the country through their conduct, professional contributions and interactions with their host communities. He described the diaspora as one of Nigeria’s valuable assets, noting that Nigerians abroad serve as cultural bridges, promoters of investment and informal ambassadors whose daily activities influence how the country is perceived internationally. The envoy specifically highlighted the entrepreneurial capacity of Abia indigenes, describing them as enterprising people with strong skills in craftsmanship, particularly tailoring and shoemaking. He encouraged them to take pride in their heritage and identity as Igbos, while using their skills, networks and economic opportunities to contribute to the development of both their host communities and Abia State. Read also: African peers offer oversight lessons for Nigeria’s $21.7bn borrowing plan Ikpeazu also called on the Valencia chapter to strengthen unity among its members, promote mutual assistance and create opportunities for collaboration that would benefit Nigerians living in Spain and communities back home. He commended the association’s leadership and members for sustaining the organisation over the past 16 years, describing its anniversary as an opportunity to reflect on its achievements and strengthen its commitment to collective development. The ambassador assured the Nigerian community that the embassy under his leadership would maintain an open and collaborative relationship with Nigerians in Spain, particularly in addressing issues affecting their welfare. He said the embassy was ready to work harmoniously with community organisations and other Nigerian groups to resolve challenges confronting citizens while strengthening people-to-people relations between Nigeria and Spain. Ikpeazu assumed office as Nigeria’s ambassador to Spain in September 2026, following the presentation of his Letters of Credence to King Felipe VI. Meanwhile, Endy Okoroafor, Chairman of Ndi Abia in Diaspora, Valencia Chapter, called for greater unity, participation and commitment among members, describing the 16th anniversary as a celebration of resilience and the collective efforts that had sustained the organisation. Okoroafor expressed gratitude to members and guests, particularly the Nigerian ambassador, for attending the celebration, noting that the association had remained united despite the challenges associated with sustaining a diaspora organisation over the years. He paid tribute to the founding members, former leaders and elders who established the association 16 years ago with the vision of creating a platform where Abia indigenes living in Spain could support one another through personal and professional challenges. According to him, the founders were driven by the desire to build a lasting institution that would promote solidarity among Abians abroad and preserve a sense of belonging for younger generations. The chairman also disclosed that the association had overcome previous challenges relating to its formal registration, announcing that Ndi Abia in Diaspora was now fully registered. He explained that the organisation was formerly known as Abia State Congress in Diaspora but encountered registration difficulties under previous administrations. Read also: 61% of students believe AI will create more career opportunities than it eliminates – Report Okoroafor said the successful registration represented an important milestone in the association’s development and would strengthen its capacity to operate as an organised platform for Abia indigenes in the diaspora. He further emphasised the need for members to uphold the Igbo principle of Onye Aghala Nwanne Ya, meaning that no one should abandon their brother, irrespective of differences in background or circumstances. He said Abians remained one people regardless of their local government areas of origin, stressing that their shared identity should continue to guide their relationships and collective activities abroad. The anniversary celebration featured cultural performances, reflections on the association’s 16-year journey, the unveiling of Almalac, presentation of awards and networking among Abia indigenes in the Valencia region.
